title: Cannabis Avocado Toast Bar for Brunch
metaDescription: Set up a build-your-own cannabis avocado toast bar where the infused olive oil waits on the side with a dose card, so each guest picks their own amount.
excerpt: Toast, avocado and a spread of toppings, with infused olive oil served on the side so every guest picks their own dose, or none at all.
keyTakeaways: Nothing gets dosed in the kitchen: the infused oil sits on the side in a labeled cruet with its own measuring spoon.
A dose card lists the estimated mg per 1/2 teaspoon, with a bottle of plain olive oil right beside it.
Toppings do the creative work: eggs, smoked fish, soft cheese, radishes, pickles and herbs.

body:
A cannabis avocado toast bar is brunch made easy: toasted bread, ripe avocados and a spread of toppings, with infused olive oil set out on the side. Nothing gets dosed in the kitchen. Each guest drizzles their own measured amount, or skips it, so a brunch for two or twenty stays in everyone's control.

## Set up a dosing station

Give the infused oil its own spot, away from the food:

- The [infused olive oil](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/) in a labeled cruet or dropper bottle, with a dedicated 1/2-teaspoon measure.
- A dose card showing the estimated mg of THC per 1/2 teaspoon, plus a reminder to start low and wait.
- A bottle of plain olive oil right beside it, so a drizzle for flavor never adds THC.

An edible can take a good half hour, or as long as two hours, to show up, so the plan is one measured drizzle and some patience. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) explains how to pick a starting amount.

## What to set out for cannabis avocado toast

Start with sturdy bread you can slice thick, about one ripe avocado for every two toasts, lemon wedges, flaky salt and pepper. Then the toppings: soft-boiled or fried eggs, smoked salmon or Michigan smoked whitefish, goat cheese or ricotta, radishes, quick pickles, cherry tomatoes, chili flakes and fresh herbs. Making your own infused oil? Browse your nearest High Society store's [menu](/shop/) for flower and order ahead for curbside pickup.

Adding an infused [berry freezer jam](/blog/canna-berry-freezer-jam/) or [super green pesto](/blog/super-green-canna-pesto/) to the spread? Label them too, and remind guests that everything infused counts toward the same dose.

## Toast, smash, drizzle

Brush the bread with plain olive oil and toast it until the edges crisp. Smash or slice the avocado at the last minute and season it with lemon, salt and pepper. Guests build their own toasts and finish with a measured drizzle of infused oil, if they want one.

## Hosting a cannabis brunch

- Keep it to adults 21+, and tell everyone up front which oil is infused.
- Make zero THC easy, with plain oil, non-infused drinks and plenty of food.
- Dose early in the day and keep it at home. Michigan law doesn't allow cannabis use in public places.
- Plan rides home. Michigan law bars driving while under the influence, and an edible can stay with you for as long as 12 hours.

For drinks, our [self-serve citrus mimosa bar](/blog/citrus-mimosa-party-with-single-strain-tinctures/) runs on the same guests-dose-themselves idea.

## After brunch

Pour the infused oil back into its labeled bottle as soon as brunch ends, and store it somewhere cool and dark that children and pets can't get to. If anyone swallows infused oil by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222. The leftover toppings are plain and go in the fridge as usual.

faq.q: How much infused oil goes on one toast?
faq.a: One measured 1/2 teaspoon or less, depending on what your dose card says it contains. Homemade oil is an estimate, so first-timers should go smaller still: about 2.5 mg of THC or less, which is around 1/4 teaspoon of an oil carded at 5 mg per 1/2 teaspoon. Eat the toast, then wait at least 2 hours before adding more. Plain olive oil is right there for extra richness.

Yes. Many cooks find that straining gently, without squeezing the plant material, and starting with a fruity olive oil keep the flavor milder. Store the oil cool and dark. At the table, lemon, flaky salt, chili and bold toppings like pickles or smoked fish balance whatever grassiness remains.

faq.q: Can I use cannabutter instead of oil?
faq.a: Yes. Melt it gently and keep it warm in a small dish with its own measuring spoon and dose card, since it firms up as it cools. It's lovely with eggs. Just don't set out infused butter and infused oil together without making clear that both count toward one dose.

ingredients: 8 thick slices of sourdough, rye or multigrain bread
Plain extra-virgin olive oil, for toasting and for the table
Infused olive oil in a labeled cruet or dropper bottle, with a 1/2-teaspoon measure and a dose card (see the dosing note)
Toppings: 4 to 8 eggs, smoked salmon or whitefish, goat cheese or ricotta, sliced radishes, quick pickles, cherry tomatoes, chili flakes, fresh herbs
steps: Set up the dosing station before guests arrive: infused oil, its measure, the dose card and a bottle of plain olive oil together, away from the food.
Cook the eggs (soft-boiled eggs hold well for a crowd) and put the other toppings in small bowls.
Brush the bread with plain olive oil and toast it in a hot skillet or a 425 °F oven until golden at the edges.
Halve the avocados just before serving and smash or slice them. Brighten with lemon, salt and pepper.
Guests build their own toasts and add a measured drizzle of infused oil only if they choose.
When brunch is over, return the infused oil to its labeled bottle and put it away.
recipe.dosingNote: **Dose card math, as an estimate:** your oil's estimated mg of THC per teaspoon ÷ 2 = mg per 1/2 teaspoon. Example: oil that works out to about 10 mg per teaspoon gets a card reading about 5 mg THC per 1/2 teaspoon. A homemade oil's real strength depends on your flower's potency and on decarboxylation and infusion losses, so mark the card as approximate. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before more, keep the bottle labeled, and keep it away from children and pets.

Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions

Michigan Judicial Institute: Traffic Benchbook, sec. 9.11, operating with a controlled substance in the body

review.summary: 18 claims checked: 16 ok, 1 wrong, 1 overstated (2 fixed). Legal lines (public use, impaired driving, 21+) match law-facts.

claims.claim: An edible can take a good half hour, or as long as two hours, to show up
claims.source: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-medication/cannabis/resources/what-you-need-to-know-if-you-choose-to-consume-cannabis.html (WebFetch): 'It can take 30 minutes to 2 hours after consumption to begin to feel the effects, but up to 4 hours to feel the full effects.'

claims.claim: An edible can stay with you for as long as 12 hours
claims.source: Health Canada page above: 'Effects can last up to 12 hours, and some residual effects could last up to 24 hours after use.'

claims.claim: Shopping list: 'about one ripe avocado for every two guests' (the recipe lists 4 avocados for 4 servings of 2 toasts)
claims.fix: now 'one ripe avocado for every two toasts', which matches the ingredient list (4 avocados, 8 toasts)
claims.source: internal consistency with recipe.yield '4 servings (8 toasts)' and ingredients '4 ripe avocados'

claims.claim: FAQ: first-timers should use around 1/4 teaspoon of infused oil
claims.fix: now tied to the dose: 'about 2.5 mg of THC or less, which is around 1/4 teaspoon of an oil carded at 5 mg per 1/2 teaspoon'; a fixed 1/4 teaspoon is only a low dose for a mild oil
claims.source: Health Canada page above: 'if you are a new consumer, look for a product containing 2.5 mg of THC or less.'; arithmetic with the dosing note's example (5 mg per 1/2 teaspoon = 2.5 mg per 1/4 teaspoon)

claims.claim: Dose card math: mg per teaspoon ÷ 2 = mg per 1/2 teaspoon; example about 10 mg per teaspoon = about 5 mg per 1/2 teaspoon, approximate
A homemade oil's real strength depends on flower potency and decarboxylation and infusion losses
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: Eat the toast, then wait at least 2 hours before adding more; start low
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'

claims.claim: Michigan law doesn't allow cannabis use in public places (keep it at home)
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-public-use: 'Using marijuana in a public place is not allowed in Michigan, and property owners may ban smoking or use on their property.' (MJI benchbook sec. 8.14, in the sources list)

claims.claim: Michigan law bars driving while under the influence; plan rides home
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-impaired-driving: 'it bans driving while under the influence' (MJI Traffic Benchbook sec. 9.11, in the sources list)
facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age: adults 21 and older; the voter law does not cover anyone under 21

claims.claim: Store infused oil cool and dark, where children and pets can't get to it
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/: 'Δ9-THC itself readily oxidizes to cannabinol (CBN) with oxygen and light'; Health Canada page above: store edible cannabis 'out of reach of children, youth, and pets.'

claims.claim: If anyone swallows infused oil by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Gentle straining without squeezing the plant material and a fruity olive oil keep canna-oil milder
claims.source: framed in the text as cooks' experience ('Many cooks find'), not as a measured result; no figure

claims.claim: Cannabutter firms up as it cools, so keep it warm in its own dish
claims.source: physical property of butter (solid at room temperature); no figure

claims.claim: Toast the oiled bread in a hot skillet or a 425 °F oven until golden
claims.source: ordinary toasting technique; no safety figure

claims.claim: Michigan smoked whitefish as a topping
claims.source: a common regional food suggestion, not a High Society product claim; no brand or store named

claims.claim: High Society: browse your nearest store's menu for flower and order ahead for curbside pickup
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering, services.curbside ('offered at every store'), services.productCategories (flower); no product named as stocked

claims.claim: Nothing is dosed in the kitchen; plain oil sits beside the infused oil; everything infused counts toward one dose
claims.source: brief angle and mustAvoid (host never pre-doses plates); guidance, no figure

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Onset and duration checked against Health Canada (WebFetch); waiting time and Poison Control against the CDC FAQ; legal lines against law-facts mi-au-public-use, mi-au-impaired-driving and mi-au-age (michigan.gov and legislature.mi.gov not re-opened, per instructions). Sources list kept: all four are https and support the text. High Society: one mention (menu for flower, curbside), in hs-facts; no consumption space, event or staff implied. Writer's notes: Host never pre-doses plates (brief mustAvoid); infused oil stays on the side. Straining tip phrased as cooks' experience, not a lab claim. High Society mentioned once (menu for flower, curbside pickup).
